Why a Moon trip starts with a gas station in space
Climbing to LEO burns most of Starship's propellant. To go on to the Moon and land, it needs full tanks, so it refills in orbit first.
A "depot" Starship launches and waits in LEO.
Tanker Starships (Starships without windows) launch one after another.
Each tanker meets the depot and moves super-cold propellant across. NASA: "similar to a gas station on Earth."
The depot fuels Starship HLS (Human Landing System), the Moon-lander version.
Super-cold (cryogenic) propellant slowly boils off. Moving it between ships at this scale has never been done. First ship-to-ship test: early 2027.
